chunks: Ali, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
He said: After the morning prayer, say: 'The Praise is for Allah, Lord of the morning. The Praise is for Allah, the Splitter of the morning,' three times.
O Allah! Open for me the door of the Command which wherein is the prosperity and the good health.
O Allah! Prepare its way for me and show me its exit.

O Allah! If You have Ordained for anyone from Your creatures capability upon me with the evil, so Seize him from his front, and his back, and from his right, and from his left, and from beneath his feet, and from above his head,
and Enshroud him with whatever You so Desire to, from wherever You so Desire to, and however You so Desire to.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite after the morning prayer for ease and protection from evil?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this supplication (du'a) from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes the concept of 'al-amr' (divine command/affair), seeking not just general ease but the specific pathway to well-being. It reflects the Shia theological emphasis on divine decree (qada') by asking Allah to preemptively remove any pre-ordained evil from all spatial directions, demonstrating a holistic reliance on God's will.
